risks: The two blocking ambiguities (Q1 account name = email, Q2 new 409 account_unavailable) carry no recorded human answer in the upstream context; T7 and T18 are built on the clarification's proposed answers and both change shape if an architect rules otherwise — a separate username means a customers column, a new sign-in identifier and an edit to a frozen request schema.

A normaliser that strips too much collapses a public host onto a denylisted parent or an internal address and starts refusing legitimate creation for every existing customer, and url_rejected is deliberately one code with one message, so nobody debugging from outside can tell which check fired (T2/T3).

InetAddress.getByName is the obvious implementation of T2 and is wrong on JDK 21: 0177.0.0.1 canonicalises to the public 177.0.0.1 while curl reaches 127.0.0.1, and 0x7f000001 / 017700000001 throw. Building on it leaves loopback bypasses open with the fix looking done.

T3 narrows POST /api/v1/links for existing authenticated callers: numeric, hex, octal and short-form IPv4 targets that return 201 today become 422, with no retroactive rescan, so the service will refuse to mint URLs it is still serving.

The lower(email) unique index (T5) fails outright on apply if the live customers table already holds two addresses differing only in case; that cannot be checked from this repository and stops the deploy mid-migration.
Without T5 landing before T6/T7, a case-variant duplicate does not fail at sign-up — it 500s the frozen sign-in endpoint later through findByEmailIgnoreCase, and would read as an unrelated incident.

shouldNotFilter is the whole access-control policy for /api/v1/*; a prefix or loose match in T10 unauthenticates link listing, editing and deletion with a green build, since no existing test asserts 401 for a token-free request against a newly exempted neighbour.

Sign-up puts a 25.6 ms, 16 MiB Argon2id hash and a database insert on an unauthenticated path whose only defence is an IP-keyed bucket that fails open when Redis is down — during a Redis outage T7 and T13 are unmetered.

Behind a proxy that does not preserve the source address, every anonymous caller shares one bucket, so the 10/min default is a global ceiling and the anonymous endpoint is effectively closed under real traffic (documented, not fixed, in T18).

Containers are JVM-wide singletons and nothing truncates PostgreSQL, so sign-up rows accumulate across the suite; duplicate tests in T7 that do not mint unique emails will collide with earlier tests rather than with the code under test.

Dropping NOT NULL on links.customer_id is one-way in production terms: re-adding it later requires deleting or re-homing every anonymous row, and the rollback plan is to stop creating them and let the TTL drain.
Both migrations (T5, T9) sit in a pipeline-protected path and will route the run to human approval; the plan depends on that approval landing rather than working around it.
During a rolling deploy the two new endpoints answer 401 or 201 depending on which pod is hit; no code fixes this, so the endpoints must be announced only after rollout completes.
